title: FedDAG: Clustered Federated Learning via Global Data and Gradient Integration for Heterogeneous Environments
claim: A multi-stage system fuses data and gradient signals to cluster clients, then trains separate primary and secondary encoders per cluster.
layout: 3 regions, numbered steps 1-9, left-to-right then downward, dashed divider
description: A system diagram split into client-side, server-side and FL training regions, with numbered blue badges 1-9 marking the order of steps. At top left, a rounded box holds client database icons. Arrows split from it to a gradient icon (a small neural net) and a data icon (stacked sheets). Both feed the server-side box. There, data and gradient are fused (neural net + data), turned into an adjacency matrix grid, then passed to hierarchical clustering (a dendrogram). Next comes client clustering, with orange Cluster 1 and green Cluster 2 ovals. The last server-side step is a cluster complementarity graph, where a blue arrow points from Cluster 2 to Cluster 1. A dashed line separates the bottom FL training row. It has two panels: Cluster 1 primary encoder training with a server, and Cluster 1 secondary encoder training that pulls gradient updates from Cluster 2. Orange and green colour-code the clusters.
caption: Overview of FedDAG. Clients compute principal vectors and gradients to build an adjacency matrix and a graph indicating which clusters can supply features for cross-cluster sharing. Training proceeds in two phases: (1) the primary encoder and classifier are trained on each cluster's local data; (2) the secondary encoder of a requesting cluster is trained on source cluster's data
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables a group of clients to collaboratively train a model without sharing individual data, but its performance drops when client data are heterogeneous. Clustered FL tackles this by grouping similar clients. However, existing clustered FL approaches rely solely on either data similarity or gradient similarity; however, this results in an incomplete assessment of client similarities. Prior clustered FL approaches also restrict knowledge and representation sharing to clients within the same cluster. This prevents cluster models from benefiting from the diverse client population across clusters. To address these limitations, FedDAG introduces a clustered FL framework, FedDAG, that employs a weighted, class-wise similarity metric that integrates both data and gradient information, providing a more holistic measure of similarity during clustering. In addition, FedDAG adopts a dual-encoder architecture for cluster models, comprising a primary encoder trained on its own clients' data and a secondary encoder refined using gradients from complementary clusters. This enables cross-cluster feature transfer while preserving cluster-specific specialization. Experiments on diverse benchmarks and data heterogeneity settings show that FedDAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art clustered FL baselines in accuracy.
